/repos/jdx/demo/pulls/1605.title: fix(complete): offer --help and --version when completing flags
/repos/jdx/demo/pulls/1605.body:
Tab completion for a CLI compiled from the derive never offered `-h`, `--help`, `-V` or `--version`, even though the parser accepts them and the help page lists them. `usage --completions zsh` had the same gap for `usage` itself.

```console
$ usage -<Tab>
# before
--completions  --usage-spec
# after
-V  -h  --completions  --help  --usage-spec  --version
```

- **`usage-argv`**: completion now offers the parser's supplied help and version flags, using the same rule the help page uses. A spelling a declared flag already took (hidden ones included) is not offered, `disable_help_flag`/`disable_version_flag` are honored, and `--version` appears only where the parser accepts it.
- **`usage complete-word`** (the reference engine, used by `usage generate completion` scripts) now offers the same implicit flags when a spec does not declare them, so both engines agree. Specs that already declare `-h`/`-V` (as `usage --usage-spec` does) are unchanged.
- **Mounts**: merging a mounted spec no longer turns `disable_help_flag`, `disable_help_subcommand` or `disable_version_flag` back off on the command that set them. Previously `mise run`, which disables `--help`, regained it from the mounted root.

Completion output for existing CLIs gains `-h`/`--help` (and `-V`/`--version` on the root), so a few expectations in the completion tests and conformance corpus were updated to include them. `cargo test --all --all-features` passes.

nodes.title: fix(complete): offer --help and --version when completing flags
nodes.body:
Tab completion for a CLI compiled from the derive never offered `-h`, `--help`, `-V` or `--version`, even though the parser accepts them and the help page lists them. `usage --completions zsh` had the same gap for `usage` itself.

```console
$ usage -<Tab>
# before
--completions  --usage-spec
# after
-V  -h  --completions  --help  --usage-spec  --version
```

- **`usage-argv`**: completion now offers the parser's supplied help and version flags, using the same rule the help page uses. A spelling a declared flag already took (hidden ones included) is not offered, `disable_help_flag`/`disable_version_flag` are honored, and `--version` appears only where the parser accepts it.
- **`usage complete-word`** (the reference engine, used by `usage generate completion` scripts) now offers the same implicit flags when a spec does not declare them, so both engines agree. Specs that already declare `-h`/`-V` (as `usage --usage-spec` does) are unchanged.
- **Mounts**: merging a mounted spec no longer turns `disable_help_flag`, `disable_help_subcommand` or `disable_version_flag` back off on the command that set them. Previously `mise run`, which disables `--help`, regained it from the mounted root.

Completion output for existing CLIs gains `-h`/`--help` (and `-V`/`--version` on the root), so a few expectations in the completion tests and conformance corpus were updated to include them. `cargo test --all --all-features` passes.

P1 **Go completion checks fail**

The new help candidates break `TestTheCursorGetsTheReferencesAnswer`. It compares `usage complete-word` with Go completion for `mise -`, `mise --`, and other flag positions. The reference now adds `-h` and `--help`, but Go's `Candidates` still returns only declared flags. Update Go completion to supply the same unclaimed built-in forms so the existing comparison keeps passing.

**Knowledge Base Used:**
- [Shell completion](https://app.greptile.com/-/switch-tenant?tenant=jdx-org&next=%2Fcustom-context%2Fknowledge-base%2Fjdx%2Fusage%2F-%2Fdocs%2Fshell-completion.md)
- [Compatibility and conformance](https://app.greptile.com/-/switch-tenant?tenant=jdx-org&next=%2Fcustom-context%2Fknowledge-base%2Fjdx%2Fusage%2F-%2Fdocs%2Fcompatibility-and-conformance.md)

P1 **Included settings no longer win**

Using `|=` in `SpecCommand::merge` changes `include` behavior, not just mounts. If a spec disables help and then includes a file with `disable_help_flag #false`, the included value previously restored help. It now leaves help disabled. The same applies to `disable_help_subcommand` and `disable_version_flag`. Keep the stay-disabled rule in the mount path rather than changing how all specs merge.

**Knowledge Base Used:** [Command model and argument parsing](https://app.greptile.com/-/switch-tenant?tenant=jdx-org&next=%2Fcustom-context%2Fknowledge-base%2Fjdx%2Fusage%2F-%2Fdocs%2Fcommand-model-and-parsing-behavior.md)

P2 **Views omit version suggestions**

Version completion still disappears through executable views. `walk_view` leaves `position.cmd` pointing at the promoted subcommand, whose generated table does not carry the root's version bit. Passing that command to `supplied_entries` omits `-V` and `--version`, although the parser uses the original root's version settings whenever a view is active. Use the parser's effective version command when supplying candidates.

**Knowledge Base Used:** [Shell completion](https://app.greptile.com/-/switch-tenant?tenant=jdx-org&next=%2Fcustom-context%2Fknowledge-base%2Fjdx%2Fusage%2F-%2Fdocs%2Fshell-completion.md)

**Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Use the view’s version settings.**

For an executable view of a versioned root, `position.cmd` is the promoted command, whose `version` is normally false. Completion omits `-V` and `--version`, although the view parser accepts them using the root settings. Use the parser’s effective version command here.
